Assessment
37-year-old male (MRN SYN-3574853) initially presented on 2024-05-28 with early disseminated Lyme disease (multiple erythema migrans, fever 38.2 C, headache, myalgias following a tick bite in Dutchess County, NY) and was started on oral doxycycline 100 mg BID.
1. Co-infection & Lab Interpretation: Baseline CBC and chemistry from 2024-05-28 are unremarkable (WBC 6.4 10*3/uL, Hgb 14.8 g/dL, Platelets 214 10*3/uL, ALT 31 U/L, Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL). Babesia microti PCR and Anaplasma phagocytophilum PCR returned negative (not detected). Therefore, co-infection testing is negative and does not change antimicrobial management (no Babesia therapy required; no evidence of cytopenias or transaminitis).
2. ECG & Clinical Significance: On 2024-06-01, the patient reported persistent lightheadedness, fatigue, and near-syncope (presyncope) while climbing stairs despite resolving fever and fading rash. Walk-in ECG demonstrated bradycardia (initial pulse 46 bpm; ECG ventricular rate 52 bpm, atrial rate 72 bpm) and second-degree AV block, Mobitz type I (Wenckebach), superimposed on severe first-degree AV block with a markedly prolonged PR interval of 340 ms (normal QRS 92 ms, QTc 420 ms).
